messages:
maria_support: Hey team — BrightBoard opened a billing dispute. Their invoice INV-1392 shows ~12.3k more billed tokens than their dashboard 'served tokens' for 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-07. Most of their traffic is realtime chat with continuous batching. Can someone triage? (account: brightboard-prod)

ashley_devex: Got it. Can you DM the request_ids or a sample CSV? Also confirm route/model (gpt-open-13b / chat.v1) and that continuous-batcher is on.

maria_support: DMed two example request_ids: r_20260302_8a7f and r_20260305_c12b. Route is /v1/chat/gpt-open-13b, continuous batcher default. Attached a CSV of ~200 rows with served_token counts.

len_infra: tagging @kai_sre — quick note: continuous batching + KV/prefix cache short-circuits often make served_tokens lower than metered. I'll pull batcher telemetry + metering gateway logs for the week.

kai_sre: Pulled metering for brightboard-prod 2026-03-01..07. billed_tokens=4,123,450, analytics served_tokens=4,111,120 => delta ~12,330. Spikes at 2026-03-02 14:12Z and 2026-03-05 09:03Z with 6x batcher concurrency.

ashley_devex: Two hypotheses: (1) duplicate metering events from retries/ingress; (2) meter event emitted pre-cache-shortcircuit and dedupe missed it. Can we grep per-request meter events for the request_ids?

len_infra: Found r_20260305_c12b. Metering shows two events for the same external id: one at gateway (pre-routing) and one when worker accepted the task — both have token_count. We dedupe by request_id downstream but saw a 30s window where dedupe key lookups returned errors due to a redis shard returning 503s. Likely some events bypassed dedupe.

maria_support: Customer also reported small latency spikes and a handful of 500s that morning — aligns with the redis/dedupe window.

billing_bot: Automated alert: Billing pipeline incident metering-20260305-isd4. Deduplication shard 4 returned 503s 2026-03-05T09:02:47Z -> 2026-03-05T09:04:13Z. Some meter events could not be deduped.

kai_sre: Reconstructed flow that causes billed > served: gateway emits meter event A on receipt; worker finds KV cache hit and serves zero tokens; normally dedupe collapses duplicates, but if dedupe is unavailable a retry or secondary event can be counted too. Net: billed > served.

ashley_devex: We should prepare a staging repro: replay customer samples with dedupe shard toggled to 503 and run continuous-batcher with KV cache enabled to reproduce double-counting. Can someone outline steps?

len_infra: Sketch repro (staging):
```
# replay sample CSV of requests (preserve X-Request-ID values)
cat brightboard_sample.csv | xargs -P50 -I{} curl -s -H "X-Request-ID: {}" -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/chat?route=chat.v1 -d @- &
# while replay runs, toggle dedupe shard 4 to return 503 for ~20s
kubectl scale deploy/dedupe-shard-4 --replicas=0 && sleep 20 && kubectl scale deploy/dedupe-shard-4 --replicas=3
```
This should show extra meter events in the pipeline for the same request ids; safer to run with sampling first.

maria_support: BrightBoard needs a mitigation now — can we credit the ~12.3k tokens while we investigate? They want an explanation and timeline for a permanent fix.

kai_sre: Proposed mitigation: one-time credit of 12,500 tokens on INV-1392 to cover the delta and mark the invoice as adjusted. Will open a billing ticket and request finance approval.

ashley_devex: Draft note for customer support: "We found a transient issue in our metering deduplication subsystem on 2026-03-05 that, combined with concurrent request patterns and continuous-batcher cache short-circuit behavior, caused a small number of meter events to be double-counted. We corrected the dedupe shard, will issue a one-time credit, and are deploying a hotfix + monitoring to prevent recurrence." Keep it short and non-technical.

maria_support: Good. Customer asked for ETA on the permanent fix.

kai_sre: ETA: hotfix (force synchronous dedupe fallback) in ~1 week; improved monitoring + rollback hooks in ~2 weeks; protocol-level idempotent meter design in 6-8 weeks. I'll add these to the incident ticket.

len_infra: Action items: (1) open billing ticket + apply credit (kai) (2) run staging repro and validate (len) (3) deploy dedupe hotfix with canary (ashley + kai) (4) send customer note and confirm credit applied (maria).

maria_support: I've told BrightBoard we will apply a credit and follow up within 48h. They'll be on a 48h update cadence. :thumbsup:

ashley_devex: I'll write a small doc for customers explaining billed vs served tokens and how cache short-circuits can look in dashboards, so this confusion is reduced. Will ping docs once wording is finalized.

kai_sre: Attaching incident ID and logs to the billing ticket. If anyone finds other accounts affected in the same window, add them to the ticket.

maria_support: Closing the loop here once the credit is applied. Thanks all."
